headline: EXPORT SALES DUE 7:30 AM; WHEAT LEADS LOWER
subheadline: Grains drift into the report window as beef import politics rattle cattle feeders.
lead: Wheat gave back 5¾ cents to $7.33 overnight, retracing Wednesday's Black Sea-driven run. Everything else barely moved. The story this morning is the 7:30 AM export sales print: with China having bought 465,000 metric tons of new-crop beans over the last two sessions, the bean number today either confirms sustained demand or tells you those sales were front-loaded positioning.
the_takeaway: Watch 7:30 AM export sales; beans above 300K MT says China demand is real, not one-off.
teaser: Export sales print at 7:30 AM CT. Beans are the tell.

one_number.unit: MT of new-crop beans sold to China in two days
one_number.context: Tuesday's sale to unknown destinations plus Wednesday's confirmed 333,000-ton Chinese purchase put two-day bean sales at 465,000 MT before today's export report prints. If today's number adds to that pace, the demand leg under November beans is real.

yesterdays_call.summary: Called beans up toward $12.47; front-month beans closed at $12.51, clearing the level by about 4 cents.
yesterdays_call.note: The call played out. Chinese demand did the work across two sessions, lifting beans through $12.47 and holding there. November beans tracked close at $12.62 -- but the scored instrument is the front contract, and it delivered.

sections.title: WHEAT GIVES BACK GAINS
sections.body:
- Chicago wheat settled at **$7.33**, down 5¾ cents, pulling back from Wednesday's 45-cent Black Sea-driven run without surrendering the whole move.
- The overnight softness is orderly: no new escalation in the Black Sea export corridor, no fresh fund liquidation signal, just position-squaring after a big session.
- Corn barely moved at $5.12 and November beans held $12.62, so grains aren't breaking together; wheat is the only one giving back, and the news that moved it hasn't reversed.
sections.catalyst: Wednesday's 45-cent Black Sea export disruption rally now partially retraced on no fresh escalation news.
sections.bottom_line: Wheat drift is digestion, not reversal. The Black Sea story hasn't changed.
sections.vs_yesterday: Wheat: Wednesday's rally partially retraced; corn and beans held ground.

sections.title: BEANS WAIT ON 7:30 AM PRINT
sections.body:
- November beans at **$12.62** are essentially flat overnight, which is what you want to see after China booked 465,000 MT over two sessions: no selling pressure selling, no give-back.
- The 7:30 AM weekly export sales report is the next real test. Under 300K MT total and the two-day China buying spree looks like front-loading; above 400K MT and the demand leg is broader than one buyer.
- The 2026 growing season's record 4.519B bushel production estimate is the ceiling on the rally; Chinese demand is the floor.
sections.catalyst: China's 333,000 MT new-crop bean purchase Wednesday, combined with Tuesday's unknown-destination sale, totaling 465,000 MT in two sessions.
sections.bottom_line: Today's export number either validates the China buying or marks it as a one-week event.
sections.farmer_action: November beans above $12.62 with export sales above 300K MT this morning: price any remaining unhedged new-crop bushels before the September WASDE resets the ceiling.
sections.vs_yesterday: Beans: two-day China buying confirmed; now waiting on export data to grade the demand.

sections.title: CATTLE: BEEF IMPORT FIGHT BREAKS OPEN
sections.body:
- Live cattle at **$218.45** barely moved, up a tenth of a percent, but the political story underneath is louder: four major livestock organizations jointly petitioned President Trump this morning to reverse a proposed 90-day beef import initiative.
- The NCBA's position is blunt: imports won't lower consumer prices, they'll undercut producer margins. That's a structural threat to a market already processing-constrained from the Cargill multi-plant lockout, ongoing since May 19, still removing roughly 6,000 head of daily processing capacity.
- Feeders at $332.57 slipped 0.4% with the Aug 24 Douglas, AZ phased reopening of Mexican feeder imports now one day away.
sections.catalyst: Four major cattle groups jointly petitioned Trump to reverse a proposed 90-day beef import initiative, published this morning.
sections.bottom_line: Beef import politics just added a new structural risk to cattle margins; watch for any White House response.

sections.title: ENERGY: HORMUZ TALKS PUSH CRUDE LOWER
sections.body:
- WTI at **$81.61** slipped 0.3% as Qatar's prime minister traveled to Tehran to discuss reopening the Strait of Hormuz, extending crude's four-session decline.
- The Iran-Hormuz cycle, a pattern of escalation and deflation that has played out twice since April, is running its familiar script: tanker struck overnight per UK Maritime Trade Operations, but diplomatic channel opened same day, and the net is a softer market, not a harder one.
- Qatar and Kuwait have restored 70% of pre-war crude exports through Hormuz via ship-to-ship transfers, removing the supply-squeeze argument.
sections.catalyst: Qatar PM traveling to Tehran for Hormuz talks; Qatar/Kuwait restore 70% of pre-war crude exports through the strait.
sections.bottom_line: Diplomatic progress is outpacing the tanker strike headlines. Diesel, not crude, stays the input-cost watch for fall fieldwork.

outside_the_pit.title: Trump Beef Import Plan Draws Unified Industry Opposition
outside_the_pit.body: Four of the nation's largest livestock groups filed a joint petition against a proposed 90-day beef import initiative Wednesday morning. For producers, this is the sharpest policy threat to fed cattle margins since the packing concentration debate; watch for a White House response before end of week.

outside_the_pit.title: USDA Workforce Gaps Are Slowing Loan and Grant Processing Nationwide
outside_the_pit.body: Farmers across the country report delays in USDA loan approvals, technical assistance, and rural housing financing as staff reductions continue. For operations carrying operating debt into harvest, slower USDA response times are a cash-flow risk, not an abstract policy complaint.

weekly_thread.question: Does Crop Progress show eastern Corn Belt condition damage from Indiana's flooding, or does the crop hold ratings through late August?
weekly_thread.status_text: Monday's Crop Progress showed a ratings dip; today's 7:30 AM export sales are the market's next data point, with the September WASDE now the next yield event. Thread resolution Friday.

the_more_you_know.title: When packers finally turn profitable
the_more_you_know.body: Drovers confirmed Wednesday that packers posted their first profitable week since April, a direct result of lower cattle purchase costs after the recent fed trade reset. That margin shift changes the bidding dynamic at the next negotiated trade: packers with positive margins have less urgency to keep bids low. Watch whether that shows up in cash cattle bids this week.

watch_list.desc: USDA Weekly Export Sales: beans above 300K MT confirms sustained demand; below 200K MT says China's two-day buying was front-loaded positioning.
Douglas, AZ phased reopening of Mexican feeder cattle imports: watch feeder/live spread for first sign of supply normalization.
USDA Crop Progress: eastern Corn Belt condition ratings; any further decline from last week's dip tightens the September WASDE setup.
White House response to the four-group joint petition against the beef import plan: any signal of reversal or confirmation moves live cattle sharply.
